Bruno is a grizzly bear appearing in the Saturday Supercade episode "Rocky Mountain Monkey Business." Prior to the events of the episode, he and his owner worked in a circus until being arrested for bank robbery. He first appears with his owner as Mr. Barkley teaches the Nature Scouts about the , the latter planning to use him to help find the money he hid before going to prison. He sends Bruno to kidnap Mr. Barkley, and they drive off to an old, abandoned ranger's cabin. At the cabin, Bruno's partner coerces Mr. Barkley into telling him why he cannot find his stolen loot, to which the latter replies that the Twin Falls River altered its course to block the entrance to Clearwater Cave. Boss Galaga is an alien species from the Namco-developed games. In this franchise, it is an enemy that uses a tractor beam to capture the player-controlled spacecraft and bring it on the enemy side. Boss Galaga is also present as an item in several crossovers with the Super Mario franchise, where it displays similar capabilities.

Alice is the queen of fairies, who appears in the Mario & Wario manga of the Super Mario Kodansha series. She is a pink fairy, she wears a red ribbon, carries a Magic Wand, and has a twin-pigtail hairstyle. She is named after the from 's novels, as hinted by her guards being playing cards. To defeat the Giant Unbaba, Chiyōrō-sama suggests using the Tottemo Oishikute Hoppe ga Ochite Shimau Kinomi located in Fairy Land. Once there, Alice appears and declares they will not part from their precious rare fruits; instead she offers Mario and his friends to depart with Fairy Land away from the planet, before the Giant Unbaba destroys it. Toxic Toad Z is one of the handful of known characters from Toad Force V mentioned in Mario Party Advance. Toxic Toad Z is a (presumably Toad-based) robotic villain in the series; more specifically, he is the henchman of the more major Spore King. When Mario, Luigi, Peach, or Yoshi accept Lantern Ghost's Nerd Force V challenge, they are directed to go to Junk, Paratroopa's item shop. On this specific mission, Junk is up and running with two items: A "Toad Force V" figurine (actually one of Jack) and a figure of Toxic Toad Z. The Super Big Tap-Tap is a gigantic monster Tap-Tap that appears in Yoshi's Island DS. It chases after Yoshi and the babies around various sections of the Island and has the ability crush dense rocks during it's rampage. Yoshi must utilize Baby Mario's dash ability in order to escape with success. The Super Big Tap-Tap is indestructible and cannot be destroyed in any way however, tossing an egg at it will cause it to appear in the Island Museum.

Giant Donkey Kong is a form of Donkey Kong. Similar to the Super form, it is an increase in size often triggered by Super Mushrooms. It has made several appearances as a boss fight in games where no other character can become gigantic.

Tetris Mario is an original transformation that Mario and Wario take in Super Mario-kun. In this form, which they can take by wearing a T-Tetrimino like a hat, they can execute a move called Tetris Flash that can zap away rows of blocks and debris. In the bonus chapter of Super Mario-kun Volume 9, Wario takes this form after destroying an underwater rock. His Goomba companion makes him notice that the rock debris are blocking their path, so Wario grabs a T-Tetrimino and executes a Tetris Flash to remove them. Afterward, in trying to pass through the rock passage, his Tetrimino headgear gets stuck in the narrow passage, forcing him to remove it. In chapter 9 of Super Mario-kun Volume 10, Wari

Ten is a member of the Extension Corps under Zokket in Mario & Luigi: Brothership alongside Ecks and Shun. He is a tall, lanky, purple miscreant whose design is based on audio connectors. His head resembles a male connector jack, giving him the general appearance of a stereotypical Japanese delinquent, and his right arm resembles a female connector socket and functions as an arm cannon. He proclaims himself as the brains of the Extension Corps and he expresses a desire to overtake Zokket as "the boss". According to one of the Grampy Turnips in the Soli-Tree, Ten is skilled at sorting out the garbage, as if he were a "recycling pro".

Super Power-Up Mario is a form Mario assumes in volume 5 of Super Mario-kun by combining various different power-ups, including the Fire Flower, Starman, Super Leaf, and Hammer Suit, resulting in a form that mixes the attributes of their associated forms: Hammer Mario, Super Mario, Fire Mario, Invincible Mario, and Raccoon Mario. The full power of this form is unknown, but Mario is able to easily defeat Koopa 3 using it. The transformation wears off once Mario, unable to control the powered-up flight, crashes on the Star World hill. The Evoglobin is the evolution of the Emoglobin and a type of creature found in Bowser's body in Mario & Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story. These live in Rump Command and ask the player to board the boats of revival so Bowser can move again and become giant when he gets knocked out. Before Mario and Luigi board the boats the Evoglobin have arms and legs.

s are a species of birds found in Donkey Kong Jungle Beat. All major Rocs found in the game are rulers of various kingdoms. All of the Rocs that Donkey Kong faces must be defeated by breaking the huge black egg they carry. The attacks the Rocs use primarily consist of firing Shadow Meteors, creating wind, and launching feathers. There are four boss Rocs: Scruff Roc, Fleet Roc, Hard Roc, and Thunder Roc. Additionally, two small enemy versions exist, the Mini Slump Bird and Gold Mini Slump Bird.

The Mushroom rebel is a Mushroom person who wears goggles and a scarf, who appears in The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! In the episode "Toad Warriors," the Mushroom rebel is shown to be a member of a rebellion against King Koopa, who has stolen all the spaghetti sauce in Car Land. The Mushroom rebel first appears when he aids Mario, Luigi, Toad, and Princess Toadstool from being captured by a State Troopa; dive-bombing the State Troopa in his helicopter, the Mushroom rebel lets down a rope ladder from his helicopter, which he tells Princess Toadstool to grab on to, which she does, after being persuaded to by Mario, Luigi and Toad. Hercufleas is a large, powerful hero who inhabits the ancient city of Mythis, and an old friend of Toad's. He is based on (also known as Heracles) of Greek and Roman legend.

Grave Tusk is the second Tusk in Donkey Kong Jungle Beat. It is the ruler of the Grape Kingdom in the GameCube version. In the New Play Control! version, it is the ruler of the Cherry Kingdom. It appears as a large, robotic elephant, colored brown, with red eyes and darker brown tusks. Grave Tusk is fought much the same way Turret Tusk and Torch Tusk are fought. At first, it has the same attacks as Turret Tusk, but after enough damage is done to it, it gains a laser attack. The only way to dodge this attack is to get into a corner that the laser will not hit. Again, Donkey Kong must throw Blood Pines at it to reveal and attack its heart. Grave Tusk is fought in VS. Grave Tusk.

Golden Mario is a form that Mario takes at the end of the Donkey Kong Country arc in Super Mario-kun Volume 15. It is a variation of the invincible form in which Mario becomes completely gold. With King K. Rool having the upper hand against the heroes, after trapping Donkey Kong in a cage, Rambi, Enguarde, and Winky comes to Mario's aid, but with the former being neutralized by a cannonball and the other two being outside their element, they pass their animal tokens to Mario, which turns him into Golden Mario. With this new power, Mario lands a punch at K. Rool's inflated belly, puncturing it and making him fly away like a popped balloon.

Dynamic Punch is a move performed by Star Mario Great in the Super Mario Bros. 4: Super Mario World 7 of Super Mario Kodansha manga. After deflecting the Kameriumu Kōsen back to Koopa Seven, Great proceeds to repeatedly punch him with his right fist., before striking the final blow.

The Debeso are legendary Yoshis that are born every millennium. They appear in Super Mario World! Yoshi no Tamago of the Super Mario Kodansha manga. They appear like Little Yoshis with wings, closed eyes, and a tuff of three hairs. Another distinctive trait, and their namesake, is the outward belly button. They are extremely intelligent, calm and have magic powers (which also includes telepathy). Every one thousand years, a Debeso is born, but at birth, the creature does not resemble the cute innocent-looking being it is known for: instead it looks like a draconian demon, but after shedding the dragon-like skin, it assumes its usual form. Dallben is one of the major characters in Disney's 1985 animated feature film The Black Cauldron. He is the greatest wizard in Prydain and the keeper of the oracular pig Hen Wen.
Crud is a giant green slime monster and the main antagonist of The New Adventures of Winnie the Pooh episode, "Cleanliness is Next to Impossible".

Clip, also known as Experiment 177, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. According to her original creation, she is designed to consume Uburnium, the most powerful and economical fuel source in the universe, and drive prices through the roof. Unfortunately, the word "Uburnium" was the same word used for "hair" in Jumba's native language. Thus, Clip instead eats hair and, if left unchecked, grows larger with all that she consumes. Her one true place is at the beauty salon as a professional hairdresser.

Charlie-27 is a Marvel Comics character that appears in Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, played by Ving Rhames. He is a member of an alien race who has superhuman strength. He is a skilled pilot and marksman, and an expert in hand to hand combat. He uses his powers and skills to protect the innocent and fight the forces of evil. He is a good friend of Yondu. Charlie-27 was created by Arnold Drake and Gene Colan.

Charoca is a magical volcanic monster who appears in the Elena of Avalor episode "All Heated Up". On the outside people have only seen him as a big bad monster, but on the inside, he is a very nice person who just has some anger issues. Whenever he loses his temper, he lets out a fiery tantrum but tries his best to keep his cool.

Carly is an antagonist and one of the nighttime villains, but sometimes an anti-hero, in the television series PJ Masks. She is one of the Speedy Twins. She first appeared in the Season 5 episode "Carly and Cartoka." She is Cartoka's twin sister and the arch-enemy of Catboy.

Cartoka is an antagonist and one of the nighttime villains, but sometimes an anti-hero, in the television series PJ Masks. He is one of the Speedy Twins. He first appeared in the Season 5 episode "Carly and Cartoka." He is Carly's twin brother and the arch-enemy of Catboy.

Catfish Booray is a recurring antagonist in the Disney XD animated series Randy Cunningham: 9th Grade Ninja. He is an insane Cajun trapper and swamp wizard who lived in the swamplands behind Norrisville High.

Captain Carter (real name Peggy Carter) is a Marvel character who first appears in the animated Disney+ series What If...? She is an alternate version of Peggy Carter, tangent from the Earth-616 universe. Captain Carter was a member of the military, fighting in World War II, when she became the subject of a serum that transformed her into a super soldier. She fought against HYDRA and the Red Skull, before being transported nearly seventy years forward in the future, through the power of the Tesseract. She eventually joined S.H.I.E.L.D. and later was chosen by The Watcher to form the Guardians of the Multiverse, a team united against the threat of Ultron, a being in possession of the Infinity

Zap, also known as Experiment 603, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to be a living laser bolt. He was captured by Gantu, but was rescued in "Snafu".

Xerek (pronounced "zer-ick") is a villain who was supposed to be the main antagonist in the 2004 Disney/Pixar animated film The Incredibles, but was replaced by Syndrome due to the latter's popularity among the producers. However, Xerek would end up retooled for use in the Boom! Studios comic book series as the villain of the ongoing story. Having an uncanny ability to always achieve victory, Xerek became an influential supervillain through his resources and influence. Extending his life through sinister means and technology, Xerek had lived for almost 200 years. Woola is a character in the film John Carter. He is a calot, the Barsoom counterpart to a dog and becomes John Carter's pet. He lives on Mars and acts somewhat like an Earth dog. He possesses super-speed and helps and protects John Carter.

Violeta "Violet" Rodriguez, also known as Ultra Violet, is the main protagonist in the Disney Channel Original Series Ultra Violet & Black Scorpion. She is a superheroine with super speed that is given to her when she puts on a magical luchador mask. She is portrayed by Scarlett Estevez.

Transylvia is the vampire-witch of the Terrified Forest in The Wuzzles. Her name is a pun of Transylvania. She is reminiscent of the winged monkeys from The Wizard of Oz or the Tengu from Japanese mythology. She travels on a flying "boomerangstick", and is proud of the fact that people are scared of her, but seems to have self-confidence issues (until the end of the episode) and turned out to not be so scary once the gang got to know her (although she dissuaded them from telling anyone). So far, she's the only Wuzzle that is a hybrid of three animals, instead of just two.

Big Bart is a legendary fish in Goldie & Bear that lives in Big Fish Lake. He was caught by Bear's uncle, but it got away. He was the target of Bear, Goldie and Mr. Bear on their fishing trip, but instead they caught his little brother Little Mike. He has grown a lot since he was caught by Bear's uncle, and is now the size of a whale.

Thena is a Marvel Comics character that appears in Eternals, played by Angelina Jolie. Thena is a member of the Eternals. She can manifest weapons from cosmic energy and is a skilled warrior and scholar. Thena was created by Martin A. Burnstein and Jack Kirby.
The Overseer (real name David Dunn) is the main protagonist of the M. Night Shyamalan films: Unbreakable and Glass. He is a superhero with super strength and the sole survivor of a train accident.

The Flying Monkeys is the name of the biker gang that serves as the Wicked Witch of the West's henchmen in The Muppets' Wizard of Oz. Formerly a rather peaceful group of "motorcycle enthusiasts", the Flying Monkeys were placed under the Witch's control when she took possession of their magic biker cap. Forced to do her bidding, the Monkeys rode their motorcycles through the skies of Oz, performing the Witch's dirty work. Once she was defeated, Dorothy returned the biker cap to Sal Minella, thereby restoring the Flying Monkeys' independence. Johnny Fiama, while associated with the Monkeys, is not formally a member of the group. He and Foo-Foo appear to be with the Witch by choice and are not

Baron Mordo (real name Karl Amadeus Mordo) is a character from Marvel Comics who appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe film Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. He is an alternate reality version of Karl Mordo who resides in Earth-838. He is part of the Illuminati and is the sorcerer supreme in this world. Baron Mordo is portrayed by Chiwetel Ejiofor, who portrayed his alternate self in the first film. Baron Mordo was created by Stan Lee and Steve Ditko.

Beauregard is the dim but lovable janitor at The Muppet Theater who took over the mantle from George the Janitor beginning in episode 310 of The Muppet Show. He also does duty as one of the stagehands, sometimes assisted by Beaker. Although he tries to be helpful, his dimwitted efforts frequently result in disaster. Affectionately known as Beau (or Bo), his slow wit is often exploited by characters who use him to their own purposes. He has a characteristic blink and often turns to the camera and says, "Right." Sproing, also known as Experiment 249, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. She is designed to use her spring-like body to launch boulders. Her one true place is helping people reach high heights.

The Silent Mary is a Spanish Royal Navy ship of the line which sailed in the Caribbean during the Age of Piracy. Commanded by Captain Salazar, she was the pride of the Spanish Navy and a fearsome pirate hunting ship. On her last mission, the Mary was wrecked in the mysterious waters of the Devil's Triangle while trying to capture the Wicked Wench. Several years later, she returned to the seas as a ghost ship. She made her debut in Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales.
The Shocker (real name Herman Schultz) is a shock-powered supervillain and an enemy of Spider-Man. Shocker was created by Stan Lee and John Romita Sr.

Sasha Baptiste is one of the main characters who appears in the supernatural teen drama series Coven Academy. Sasha is a student at Crescent Veil Academy and a friend of Briar and Tegan. She is a powerfully empathetic witch who can read emotions and control thoughts, but remains cautious of outsiders due to a painful family history.
Saloso is a shapeshifting malandro and the main antagonist in the Elena of Avalor episode "The Tides of Change".

Captain America (real name Samuel "Sam" Thomas Wilson, formerly known as Falcon) is a superhero from Marvel Comics who appears in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He made his cinematic debut in Captain America: The Winter Soldier as a former Air Force pilot and veteran who had used an advanced flight harness equipped with mechanical wings but had retired following the death of his friend and partner Riley. However, when HYDRA had emerged from infiltrating S.H.I.E.L.D. and planned to murder thousands of people, Sam re-donned his wings and suit, becoming the Falcon and allying with Captain America to stop them. He has since joined the Avengers. He continues to act as an ally and the partner of C

Romeo is the main antagonist of the Disney Jr. show PJ Masks. He is one of the nighttime villains. Flying in his sky factory above the city or driving around in his lab, this crazed scientist and inventor is bent on nothing less than world domination.

Rey, later self-proclaimed Rey Skywalker, is the protagonist of the Star Wars sequel trilogy. A lone scavenger abandoned as a child on the desert planet Jakku, she gets tangled in the war between the Resistance and the First Order after deciding to help the droid BB-8. She uncovers her potential as a Force-user while on her quest to seek out the sole existing Jedi, Luke Skywalker, to save the galaxy. During her journey, she develops an intimate and intricate relationship with the central antagonist, Kylo Ren (whose real name is Ben Solo), the son of Princess Leia and Han Solo. Prince Phobos is a character from W.I.T.C.H. He rules as prince over Meridian while searching for his sister to kill her for her power; she is the rightful heir to the throne of Meridian. Phobos is considered an immortal and may be thousands of years old. He spends most of his time in the confines of his castle, only granting audiences to those he deems worthy to see his face. Phobos' devious plan is to absorb the immense magical powers of his long-lost sister, Elyon, and the only ones standing in his way are the five Guardians of Kandrakar.

Plasmoid, also known as Experiment 617, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to attack by firing balls of plasma from his scorpion-like tail. He was captured by Gantu, but was rescued in "Snafu".

Peter Pegasus (also known as Baby Pegasus or Young Pegasus in certain sources) is a character in "The Pastoral Symphony" segment of the 1940 film Fantasia. He is presumably the youngest of his siblings, and bears the most resemblance to his parents, having his father's coat and his mother's mane, tail, and eye color. He is a playful little foal, eager to get in on the fun, and fly with his family. The character's popularity within the Disney studio lead them to consider utilizing him in future Fantasia segments before work on any Fantasia followups were cancelled.

Periwinkle is a frost-talent fairy from the Winter Woods and Tinker Bell's younger twin sister. She appeared in Secret of the Wings, and is one of the two protagonists, and makes a minor appearance in The Pirate Fairy.

Jeffrey Mace is a Marvel Comics character who appears in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., played by Jason O'Mara. He is the new Director of S.H.I.E.L.D. and disguises as an Inhuman with super-strength. Jeffrey Mace was created by Ray Gill and George Mandel.

Najma is a character from Marvel Comics, who appears within the Marvel Cinematic Universe. She made her debut in the second episode of the Disney+ series, Ms. Marvel. She is portrayed by starring cast member, Nimra Bucha. Najma is the mother to Kamran, and a member of the Clandestines. She is a Djinn, originating from the Noor Dimension, who was exiled to Earth, and has been searching a way to return home, ever since. After Kamala puts on her great-grandmother's bangle, she is plagued with visions of Najma, who seeks her out, in hopes that she possesses the power to help them return to their home. When Kamala expresses doubts in helping her return, Najma briefly pursues her, before she is ar
Morgana Le Fay is a powerful ancient sorceress and the overarching antagonist of the 2010 Disney film The Sorcerer's Apprentice.

Moon Knight (real name Marc Spector, also known as Steven Grant/Mr. Knight and Jake Lockley) is a fictional character appearing in comic books published by Marvel Comics. Moon Knight is empowered by Khonshu, the Egyptian god of the Moon. This gives him superhuman strength. Besides that, he is an expert at boxing and martial arts and a great combat strategist. Moon Knight was created by Doug Moench and Don Perlin.

The Mayoi are an artificially created plant-fungi animal hybrid created by Sycorax in Big Hero 6: The Series. Though small and adorable, they can grow to become vicious monsters that Mr. Sparkles can control.

Man Baby (real name Timmy Grubbs) is a character from the Disney Channel animated series Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur. He is the infant son of a brilliant scientist, who became a giant after messing with his father's experiment, becoming a supervillain.

Mangani is a great spirit ape from The Legend of Tarzan episode "Tarzan and the Silver Ape". He is the healing spirit of the jungle. He wanders the jungle curing the sick and the wounded animals in need of healing with the help of the full moon's light which gives him his powers.

Madame Web (real name Julia Carpenter) is a superhero from Marvel Comics that appeared in Ultimate Spider-Man, voiced by Cree Summer. A teenage psychic, she was Nick Fury's secret asset and has been protected by him ever since Hydra took over the TriCarrier. As it turns out, she has been with Nick Fury and Nova ever since they went missing. Julia Carpenter was created by Jim Shooter and Mike Zeck. Madame Web was created by Dennis O'Neil and John Romita Jr.
Luis Madrigal is one of the main characters in the film Descendants: Wicked Wonderland. He is the son of Luisa Madrigal from Encanto and shares his mother's powers of super strength.

The Liquidator (real name Bud Flud) is a recurring antagonist of the Darkwing Duck franchise. He was a crooked bottled water salesman that fell into a reservoir he had contaminated, turning him into a mutant dog-like creature with the power to assume a viscous form and control water who constantly speaking in advertising-styled lingo. He is additionally a member of Negaduck's Fearsome Five.
Jiaying is a Inhuman gifted with longevity after experiencing Terrigenesis. She serves as the main antagonist of the second season of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.

The Jaquins are magical flying creatures that appear in the Disney Channel series Elena of Avalor. They are a cross between a jaguar and a macaw and are known as the guardians of Avalor sworn to protect the kingdom from dark forces that would threaten it. Due to Shuriki's invasion, they were reluctant to trust foreigners such as Sofia until Elena was restored to power.

Jack Frost is the main antagonist in Disney's 2006 live-action film The Santa Clause 3: The Escape Clause, the second sequel to the 1994 film. He is the legendary figure responsible for snow, ice, and cold weather. As a legendary figure, he is a member of the Council of Legendary Figures, though he hardly ever shows up at council meetings.

Jack Skellington is the protagonist of Tim Burton's 1993 stop-motion Disney and Touchstone film The Nightmare Before Christmas. He is the "Pumpkin King" of Halloween Town. Jack Skellington is the patron spirit of Halloween, portrayed as being on par with Santa Claus and the Easter Bunny within his own holiday. As a living skeleton, he is immortal and can remove parts of his body without harm, as is often demonstrated for comic relief. He is the most important of many Halloween spirits, with the implication that their job is to scare people in the real world on Halloween night, though all in innocent fun.

Iron Hulk (real name Amadeus Cho) is a Marvel Comics character who is one of the main protagonists of the Disney Jr. animated series Iron Man and his Awesome Friends. He is a member of the Iron Friends who wears a suit of armor that gives him super-strength. Together with her friends Iron Man and Ironheart, he protects the city as Iron Hulk. Amadeus Cho was created by Greg Pak and Takeshi Miyazawa.

Ironheart (real name Riri Williams) is a superheroine from Marvel Comics, who dons a high-tech suit of armor modeled after Iron Man. She made her live-action debut in the 2022 Marvel Cinematic Universe film Black Panther: Wakanda Forever, headline Ironheart, and set to return in Armor Wars. Ironheart was created by Brian Michael Bendis and Mike Deodato.

Isis Vanderchill is an antagonist from Darkwing Duck franchise, that debuted in "All's Fahrenheit in Love and War". Formerly known as the "Ice Queen of St. Canard", Isis is a vain duck and the owner of the Vanderchill Ice Factory who in an attempt to stop herself from aging, underwent an experimental treatment to freeze her face, only to have her blood frozen instead, which granted her ice-based powers and the inability to experience warmth.

Huckleberry Knucklehead is a character in Wander Over Yonder. He is a giant baby that first appeared in "The Toddler". He is voiced by Owen Faust, the nephew of producer and story editor Lauren Faust.

Huggo, also known as Experiment 489, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to use his tentacles to squeeze the life out of his victims.

Hua Mulan is the titular protagonist of the 2020 live-action remake of Mulan. She is a young woman who runs away from her home in order to serve the Chinese army. She uses the alias Hua Jun while pretending to be a boy and is the first soldier to carry two buckets of water up a mountain without spilling any. She exposes herself when in battle she had to take off her armor, to properly use her chi powers. She is based on both the character from Chinese legends and the character of the same name from the 1998 animated film.

Heat, also known as Experiment 609, is an illegal genetic experiment created by Jumba Jookiba and a character in the Lilo & Stitch franchise. He is designed to fire orange heat lasers from the black oval-shaped bulb on his forehead. He was captured by Gantu, but was rescued in "Snafu".

Gravitas is a character from the Disney Channel animated series Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur. He is a supervillain whose gloves can shoot liquid that negates targets' gravity. Gravitas was created by Kevin Grevioux and Paco Medina.

Gravitina is a recurring antagonist in the Disney/Pixar animated series Buzz Lightyear of Star Command. The self-proclaimed Mistress of Gravity, Gravitina has the ability to control gravitational fields with her massive cranium. She has a crush on Buzz Lightyear and her schemes often involve futile efforts to win his affection. She is voiced by Kerri Kenney.

Ginorma is an antagonist in The 7D season 2 episode "Game of Grumpy". A giant woman, she was soon to be King Groucharooney's bride, until she was part of a plot to overthrow Grumpylvania with the ice stormers, and she revealed herself as the Ice Queen from Beyond the Fence.

Fashoom is an evil giant cyclops with an eye of destructive power who appeared in the Aladdin episode "The Prophet Motive". He also made cameos in "Caught by the Tale" and "Sneeze the Day". He is Fasir's younger brother.

The Elementals are a sequence of illusions that appear in Spider-Man: Far From Home. They are based on the Marvel Comics characters of the same name. They are apparitions created by the evil genius Mysterio to help him further his schemes, each embodying one of the four elements of nature, hence their name. The four are created to appear as if they have complete control over fire, lava and magma, water, sand, air and wind, respectively. The Elementals were created by Jenny Blake Isabella and Val Mayerik.
Yannik is a giant Hyena Beast from Ikoria. Its bonder is Nikara.

Tam, originally named Tamira by her creator Jace Beleren, is a gorgon. Jace conceived of her as his perfect protégé, an ally who possessed his best qualities and was his equal in magecraft and telepathy. However, she grew into her own independent being, and sought a path forward outside of Jace's designs. When Jace died, he gifted her his planeswalker spark, making her the first attested Planeswalker to ignite after the Desparkening.

The Speed Demon is a lesser demon of Duskmourn, released by Valgavoth to chaperone Winter. It races among the possessed and the damned as a demonic minder, the tormentor of the Speed Demons team captain, Winter.

The unnamed Dominarian golem that was nicknamed "Boom" was used by the men of Captain Hask as a form of siege engine and heavy duty fighter sometime after the Phyrexian Invasion. He once helped defeat a group of Yotian Soldiers and later fought against the dragon Zumaki.

Greta Gorunn is a first-year dwarf student at Lorehold College in Strixhaven University. Loud, cheerful, and endlessly energetic, she is a well-known presence on campus both for her physical strength and her irreverent sense of humor.

Barrow and Zeph are a bonded human-monster pair native to the plane of Ikoria. Barrow is a young man who appears to be a skilled bonder, capable of communicating with and understanding the intentions of his companion, Zeph. Zeph is a massive cat-clade monster, distinguished by his large size, striped appearance, and control over electricity. Together, Barrow and Zeph were part of a coalition attempting to investigate and potentially stop the corruption surrounding the Ozolith, a powerful crystalline structure influencing monster behavior. The pair is known for their composed demeanor and willingness to cooperate with other bonders, hunters, and outsiders when necessary.
King Yorvo is a giant noble and the former ruler of Garenbrig on Eldraine.
Wasitora was the queen of the nekoru cat-dragons on Dominaria. She was one of only three nekoru who had natural green-mana healing abilities. Her name means "Eagle Tiger."

Lady Verdenth was a green mana sorceress and mistress of House Verdenth in Arathoxia and lady of the forest of Krysalthus on Corondor She saved the infant Jared Carthalion in Krysalthus from wolves as Ezer rushed the baby away from the Battle of Aster Fall. She allied with Marshal Bikov during Ravidel's invasion of Arathoxia, until Ravidel killed her.

Agnomakhos was the leader of the Archon tyrants of Theros, who ruled for hundreds of years over Trax, a massive empire of centaurs, humans, leonin, minotaurs, and satyrs in ancient times. Agnomakhos used the leonin as an army, and ruled a particularly brutal regime centered in modern Meletis that extended into the mountains to the north and the forests to the east, using the pretext of a war against the giants to legitimize his rule. Eventually, the empire of Trax fell to a rebellion led by kings Kynaios and Tiro, and the first polis, Meletis, was born from its ashes. When leading his forces, Agnomakhos rode a flying bull into battle.
Tover Giants-Blood is a giant human warrior, who faced down the much smaller Arni Brokenbow and lost.

Baltrice is a red-aligned planeswalker, at least 6 feet tall with broad shoulders and ash-grey hair. She is the loyal lieutenant of the artificer Tezzeret, working for the Infinite Consortium. Being a pyromancer, she specializes in fire elementals though she seems to have learned some of the art of artifice from Tezzeret.
Nevinyrral was a lich and necromancer from Urborg on Dominaria. He also was the author of the Necromancer's Handbook, the bible of necromancy.

Mina and Denn are a pair of twin elves of the Mul Daya tribe of Zendikar. Mina is what is known as a Greenweaver, able to channel the essence of their ancestors and their bond with nature into raw magical power.
Kothophed was one of the four demons who dealt with Liliana Vess following the Mending. He bestowed upon Liliana eternal youth, carved into her skin as intricate tattoos.

Kolo Meha was a pyromancer of tremendous power from Dominaria, with a good, if slightly destructive, sense of humor. He had reached the level of sixth-circle mage (out of ten) in his native Bogardan. To advance beyond that he had to make a pilgrimage, a journey around the world to learn how to use his powers in places that were not as vibrant with red mana as Bogardan was.

The Khalni Heart is a magical flower that is an outgrowth of the soul of Zendikar. Led by visions, the Zendikari planeswalker Nissa Revane traveled into the depths of the devastated continent of Bala Ged to find the Khalni Heart which apparently had grown a new bud there. Rumors said that it had come to revive the land after the onslaught by the Eldrazi. Through it, Nissa rekindled her connection to the plane — but she also ran afoul of the demon Ob Nixilis, a former planeswalker who hoped to use the power of the Khalni Heart to reignite his spark. Flush with the elemental power of Zendikar, Nissa bested Ob Nixilis, removed the Khalni Heart to safety, and escaped.

Jodah is a powerful archmage from Dominaria, who was mostly present during the Dark Age and Ice Age for many of the important historical events on Terisiare during the period. He made a habit of gathering nicknames and epithets along his travels, most notably Jodah the Eternal.

Derevi Empyrial tactician is a legendary bird wizard from Bant, on Alara. While she soars above the battlefield, Derevi uses cunning strategies to outsmart her enemies. She orchestrates the movements of her great army as they fight invaders who would lay waste to the peaceful lands of Bant. Derevi's keen eyes can absorb a multitude of factors as she rapidly alters her plan to meet the changing conditions on the ground. Her devoted followers consider Derevi the greatest commander the Shards have ever seen. Thanks to her brilliant strategy, the Grixis hordes were routed at the Battle of Split Peak. Her clever diplomacy diverted the Esper Council in their plot against her. Derevi is disciplined

Akiri, Aki to her friends, is a legendary Kor warrior and ally from Zendikar. She is arguably the greatest line-slinger on Zendikar, blazing new trails and surviving falls that would prove fatal to anyone else.

The Seismic Talus is the boss of the Suthorn Ruins in and is the second overall boss of the game. This formidable adversary is a massive rock-like creature with a glowing purple core that players must target to defeat it.
Invincible Body Báilóng (不死身胴 白龍 Fujimidō Byakuryū) is a character from Tatakae!! Ramenman.

Xehanort, also known as Master Xehanort, is a major character in the Kingdom Hearts series and the central antagonist of the Dark Seeker Saga. Xehanort is the main playable character of Kingdom Hearts Dark Road, which takes place during his youth and explores his journey to becoming the Seeker of Darkness. Xehanort is a Keyblade Master, a descendent of Ephemer, and a former teacher to Ventus. He believes that darkness and light should exist in perfect balance, and for this reason, he seeks to conquer Kingdom Hearts and recreate the worlds according to his wishes. It is used by Riku, Riku Replica, Anti-Riku, Vanitas, and Terra to fire a ball of dark flame toward a target. In Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep it has the potential to blind enemies when hit.

Kaku catches his opponent's by their arms, then tosses them onto his leg as he brings his knee up and finishes this move by slamming the back of his fist into the opponents head, effectively crushing their skulls.

Agaard inhales and suddenly enhances his muscular strength (his muscles are visibly being buffed) via using his special breathing, then he jumps at his opponent raising his arm and delivers a powerful elbow strike.

The is a heavy unit, towering above other the standard Voteless. Mutated into a towering giant, this creature carries a massive mace which may look slow, but its swings are deceptively quick.

A Slotto (pronounced 'Slowtow') is a mighty beast common to both Eternia and Etheria. Large and furry, Slotto's are easily domesticated and often used as beasts of burden by humans. A task often appointed to the creatures is pulling wagons. Slotto's come in various different shades of purple and lilac. Once, a purple furred Slotto owned by a young Eternian peasant boy was pulling a cart up a hill when the chain attaching the cart to it broke and the wheeled vehicle began rolling down the hill at increasing speed. The Snake Goddess is an Eternian deity and watches over the Snake Men, whom she calls her "children". She appears to be a spirit of a beautiful woman with snakes instead of hair like the mythological Medusa. She seems to be immortal because she names He-Man as "mortal". After the Snake Men are defeated in one occasion, she vanishes but threatens He-Man with her return.
Plasmar is a member of the Heroic Warriors who possesses the ability to use his plasma-based powers to replicate the weapons of his enemies. He is an archenemy of Camo Khan.

Ogres are a race of monstrous humanoids native to Eternia. They are large, powerful, and aggressive. There are at least two different species of ogres, which vary in appearance and personality. The Vine Jungle is home to ogres that resemble Bakull. They are solitary creatures that are not shown to be capable of speaking or using tools. In contrast, a mountain between Baron Grod's fortress and the Royal Palace is home to a tribe of ogres that more closely resemble oversized orks. They are capable of speech and employ advanced weapons and technology, including laser rifles and one-man flying ships.
Krytis Birds are pterodactyl like flying beasts that live on the planet Krytis, specifically on the island of Mondor.

West-Star Horses is an animal from the animated series The New Adventures of He-Man. West-Star Horses were gleaming silver robotic animals. they resided in the stables with organic animals, and during their act were ridden by cowboys as they entered the arena to the applause of the gathered spectators, lifted off and began to fly.

B-054-846 was the codename of a Brute War chieftain. He reportedly killed 23 UNSC Marines before being neutralized by Lance Corporal T. B. Williams, who scored a long-range sniper kill. ONI is currently cross-referencing this Brute Chieftain's identifiers against those recorded in previous Brute encounters. He appears to wield a hammer similar to the Fist of Rukt.
Pluton is a genetically modified Jiralhanae designed to counter the strength of the Spartans. Pluton is a non-canon character that was presented in the anime short Odd One Out in Halo Legends.

Mgalekgolo (Ophis congregatio, meaning "serpent union"), more commonly known as Hunters, are a unique gestalt of smaller creatures known as Lekgolo, which are orange, worm-like creatures. Lekgolo were known to group together and form a Mgalekgolo for protection during combat, due to the form's increased strength at the cost of maneuverability. When grouped together, the intelligence of the Mgalekgolo colony is increased with every additional Lekgolo.

Rangmejo (as they were known to Forerunner Lifeworkers), or "quadwings", are a species of large interplanetary pterosaur-like creatures with dual sets of wings. They are among the most ubiquitous varieties of fauna that have been encountered on Forerunner installations by the United Nations Space Command, as they have been observed on Installation 00 and multiple Halo rings. At least two subtypes have been observed. Rangmejo have been known to gather in significant numbers within artificially-constructed chambers.
King Yorvo is a giant noble and the former ruler of Garenbrig on Eldraine.

Zilgeth was the leader of Clan Ruby in Storgard in the Ice Age of Dominaria. When a Johtull Wurm attacked Storgard he sacrificed himself to fend off the creature with an Incinerate spell. After his death and burial, Freyalise became the new leader of Clan Ruby.

The Windgrace Acolytes are a Dominarian order of cat warriors on Urborg, who follow the anti-artifact principles of Lord Windgrace. They are vigilant against the spread of Phyrexia, and fly on pterodactyl-like creatures. It is said that they bear the memory of the war like soldiers bear battle scars. Founded after the Phyrexian Invasion, they tended the Heroes' Memorial and used trained insects, called gladehunters, to track down artifice and artificers alike. They tried to discourage Venser from working on his ambulators. After the coming of the Cabal and the Memorial's destruction by Belzenlok, the Acolytes fought to keep Urborg relics out of Cabal hands.

Will Kenrith is a former planeswalker who specializes in ice magic, and the current acting king of Eldraine. He is the twin brother of Rowan Kenrith. His other siblings are Erec and Hazel, his father was High King Algenus Kenrith, and his stepmother was Queen Linden. Through his biological mother, he is the nephew of the witches Agatha, Eriette, and Hylda. He and his twin sister lost their shared spark as a result of the Desparkening.
Wasitora was the queen of the nekoru cat-dragons on Dominaria. She was one of only three nekoru who had natural green-mana healing abilities. Her name means "Eagle Tiger."
Atsushi is a dragon spirit from Kamigawa. She is the reincarnation of Ryusei.

Tarem is a Dimir agent on the plane of Ravnica. Tarem is a notion thief, able to steal thoughts, memories, and experiences from both the living and the deceased. His eyes and grin are sharp and bright, and he wears mildly extravagant clothing. He appears to be a young man, but his true age may be far older than what it appears.

Snapdax, the All-Hunter is the apex monster of the Savai triome on Ikoria. This ferocious hunter lives in a cavern lair, which is adorned by the trophies from its kills, in a twisted show of justice, since usually humans are the ones who display their hunting trophies. The planeswalker Vivien Reid stumbled upon the cavern full of skulls while exploring the mesa of Savai. Vivien managed to flee from the rapidly waking Snapdax only thanks to her fast-moving . Snapdax is an unrivaled predator, combining cat-like cleverness and nightmarish stealth with dinosaur aggression. It can be said that it is the most efficient killing machine. Revin Skoros is a criminal Zombie Wizard on Alara. He has had various aliases including Dead Reckoner, The Anathemancer, and Ol' Flame Eyes. He has been wanted for the corruption of mana bonds in three shards, consumption of the flesh of the living, consumption of the flesh of the dead, assault, arson, and unauthorized tissue reanimation in a holy zone.

Mochi, the Smiling Kami of the Crescent Moon, was a powerful yet diminutive kami who attempted to manipulate Toshiro Umezawa, while secretly working with the Soratami to make them the dominant species in the plane Kamigawa.
Liches are beings who have stored their life force in an object called a phylactery so that their mortal body will endure upwards of millennia in undeath.

Jhoira (JOY-ruh) is a nearly immortal Shivan artificer of the Ghitu tribe who studied at the Tolarian Academy on Dominaria.
Syr Imodane is a Human woman and pyromancer from Eldraine. She briefly declared herself Queen.

Jegantha, the Wellspring is a legendary elemental elk from the plane of Ikoria. Jegantha is mana incarnate. This monster seems to amplify every and any magic cast in its vicinity. The planeswalker Vivien Reid tried a simple enlarging spell on a beetle, which assumed truly colossal dimensions. Vivien wonders what could Jegantha do if it should have a bonder. Jegantha fought in defense of Ikoria during New Phyrexia's Invasion of the Multiverse.
Holger Burk was a silversmith who became a werewolf, on the plane of Innistrad.

Hypatia was trained as a grange-mage in a Meletian temple to Karametra, but found that her calling was on the field of battle. She took up the sword and shield of the Meletian army and showed great promise in fighting off threats to the city. During one battle, she was wounded on a high plateau overlooking Meletis. She saw a pegasus herd flying overhead and said a silent prayer. A pegasus flew down and allowed her to climb onto its back, saving her life. The two of them became inseparable.

Hidetsugu (hee-DET-soo-goo; ), also called the Scourge of Minamo was an ogre o-bakemono, a shaman from Kamigawa. He lived in the Sokenzan mountain range in a cave dwelling named Shinka. He was a master of blood and fire magic, and a devout worshipper of the All-Consuming Oni of Chaos, therefore highly skilled in working with oni demons. He had quite a simple philosophy: everything is doomed to end in chaos, consumed by his master. In the end, he merged himself with the oni, becoming a formidable power.

Halfdane (also Dane) was a shapeshifter from Dominaria that was obsessed with his reflection. He was more intelligent than the who, like he, came from ancient Tolaria. Halfdane was a mentally unstable killer, responsible for the deaths of Kei Takahashi, Barktooth Warbeard, Ragnar, and (presumably) Ramirez DePietro.

Giada is a teenaged girl and the youngest angel on New Capenna. At the Cabaretti Crescendo, she was revealed to be The Font, a new source of Halo. She sacrificed herself to save Elspeth Tirel and was revived with Halo during New Phyrexia's Invasion of the Multiverse.

Eliza, known as Eliza of the Keep, was a young human woman from Alara, dwelling on the shard of Grixis and the only still-living Necromancer baron of the plane. Her skin was pale and supple, but her neck had a faint purple hue to it, possibly from some past injury. She ruled as baron of the Keep at Ilsun Gate in the Dregscape, and later of Unx itself. Eliza routinely requires the vis of the living to retain her vitality, so her legions are constantly scouting for villages and raiding ogre lairs.

Fetra is an enemy character from Fire Emblem: Genealogy of the Holy War. She is one of the members of Duke Bloom's sister magi squad, consisting of herself, Vampa, and Eliu. Each of the sisters specialize in a particular type of magic, Fetra's being Wind. The three sisters appear in both Chapters 7 and 8, and will die in the latter chapter while facing off against Seliph's army.

St. Elimine was one of the Eight Legends who fought in The Scouring, wielding the light tome Aureola and the healing staff known as the Staff of the Saint. Since she possessed strong faith, she was framed as a Saint (聖女, Seijo lit. Holy Woman) after The Scouring. Elimine went on to found the country Etruria and the St. Elimine Church.
The Children of the Goddess, also known as Nabateans, are a race of dragons in the Fódlan Series of Fire Emblem.
Dusk is a wildhunt shifter and Inspector in the Sharn Watch who is on the payroll of the Boromar Clan.
Calmachia is a unique living construct resembling the form of a dragon based at a Cannith creation forge in the Mournland, on the border with Darguun.
A behir is a great serpentine monster with twelve legs and electrical breath.
Chaos rocs are gargantuan predatory birds with rainbow plumage, and the ability to blast prismatic spray from their eyes.
Hell hounds are fiendish fire-breathing dogs native to the plane of Fernia.
Gorgons are powerful bull-like creatures covered in iron plates. They can be found underneath Eberron in the caverns of Khyber.
Gennara ir'Damilek is a half-elf silver pyromancer who is the head of the informal college of silver pyromancers within the Order of the Pure and leader of the Order overall.

Grell are sightless aberrations that resemble giant floating brains with tentacles and a beak. Originally from the plane of Xoriat, grells are unusual in that they were not introduced to Eberron by the daelkyr.

A harpy is a monstrous humanoid creature known for its entrancing voice and ability to fly. Harpies travel in flights, with most of the flights living in Droaam under the rule of the Daughters of Sora Kell.
Gatesmasher is a massive clay golem found in Shavarath, built for destroying fortifications. During the Codex War, Gatesmasher wandered the battlefield in the shadow of the Tower of Despair.

Abu Zide was a legendary figure who was said to have traveled in a frigate which defied the Spacing Guild by riding "there" and back in a day. Used in this way, "there" derives from Fremen mythology, meaning "the land of the ruh-spirit, the alam al-mithal where all limitations are removed.". The Commentaries drew a parallel between Abu Zide and the Kwisatz Haderach, the latter being "one who can be two places simultaneously".
Slarpons were scaly jungle creatures from Rossak with needle teeth and thick body armor. They stayed in predatory perches

Soul of Crota is a Hive major and the final boss of The Wakening. It is capable of summoning Hive reinforcements and launching energy blasts. After a long fought battle, a Guardian finally manages to banish Crota's soul.

They are able conjure crescent-shaped projectiles that suspends targets caught in the path and enrage nearby Dread units. More powerful Harbingers are resistant against non-Strand damage sources. They are identified by the slim frame, yellow lines covering their face and a green uniform on their body.

Fikrul, the Fanatic is the Archon of the Scorn, a race of undead Eliksni, and the leader of its Barons. He calls Uldren Sov father, likely believing him to be the source of his power. Due to his resurrection ability, Fikrul can seemingly never truly be killed, and has retorted that he will continue to return to seek vengeance upon the Guardian.

Either as a gambit to compel the Hive to surrender or to avenge the loss of Primus Ta'aun, Tlu'urn and Mau'ual breach the Dreadnaught's power core and threaten to destroy it, which would destroy the Hive vessel and take most of the Solar System with it. For those who face Valus Tlu'urn, he wields a massive back-mounted Arc-cannon which delivers a payload so powerful the Vanguard estimates Tlu'urn could face a Goliath Tank himself.

Sylok both reveled in the pain and used it to feed his Worm. Sylok would survive his encounter with the Guardians and join forces with the Dread several years later. He would encounter the Guardians once again, who were seeking out Fikrul, the Fanatic within the now Tomb of Elders.

Mind flayers, also known as illithids, are aberrations with potent psionic abilities. On Critical Role, they have so far only been encountered in the realm of the Underdark.

Kaldon Thunderhead was a legendary stormborn half-giant hero. He was born beneath a raging storm, like many other stormborn, and eventually he manifested storm powers and became a mighty warrior. One of his great feats was slaying the "ember roc of the south in single combat.

Gold dragons are powerful, wise, aloof true dragons who dwell in out-of-the-way, temperate places, often near water features. Older gold dragons sometimes assume humanoid or beast forms to engage in brief, benign interactions with people. No confirmed gold dragons have yet been named or appeared in Critical Role stories.

Ganix, the Laughing Hand, was the Undying Chosen of the Crawling King: one of the god's most loyal and most powerful zealots. As an NPC, Ganix was played by Matthew Mercer.
Balsaad was a mighty river dragon. He turned rogue by joining with the spirit known as the Lord of the Locust. He was killed by Rose after being hacked into pieces.
